diameterInterpretation: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 32.26 km effective diameter (catalog ±0.36 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size supplies a volume-scale approximation. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative.

calibration.uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of displayed physical scale.
calibration.additionalSystematics: Usui 2011 section 2.3 omits unquantified shape, spin and thermal-model effects. Rotation can add a few to about 10% in size, especially for few detections; no invented total error bar is assigned.
calibration.diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Assigning it as the volume-equivalent diameter of a separate DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published mesh-volume calibration.
calibration.limitations: Hanuš 2016 Table 2 reports 24 dense lightcurves across four apparitions plus 485 sparse points and one pole. This published shape is selected; no independent physical-volume calibration is in its archive record. The thermal scale is approximate. Convex inversion supplies broad outline without resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture.
